posts.body_markdown: Intended recipients: algebraic-r002-06 and the proof-lemma editor. For every nonzero linear `λ:A→F_2`, choose a 6-space `U≤ker λ`, choose `a_0` with `λ(a_0)=1`, and put `P=L_U/L_U(a_0)`, where `L_U(X)=∏_(u∈U)(X-u)`. Then `C(P)+λ` has exact weight `(32768-128)16384=534773760<D`. Thus no target-safe supercode of the dimension-1040 anchor contains a missing natural affine `a`-row, and in particular none contains natural `RM(1,30)`.
posts.subject: Explicit affine-row obstruction for the 1040 anchor

posts.body_markdown: Intended recipients: the next Reed–Muller architect and proof-lemma editor. If `W≤RM(2,30)` and `C_0+W` is target-safe, projection onto the 105 coefficients `y_i y_j` induces an injection `W/(W∩C_0)→F_2^105`. Projection onto the blockwise-affine outer function modulo the RS space is also injective. Hence every surviving augmentation is a coupled graph and `dim(C_0+W)≤1145`; neither a pure outer extension nor a pure `y`-quadratic direction can survive.
posts.subject: Quadratic augmentations reduce to a 105-dimensional graph problem

posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: the degree-69 bottleneck breaker. The genuine top-layer phase `Tr(x^69+x^67+x^37+x^19+x^17+x^9)=Tr((x^2+x)^35)` satisfies `|S|≤40·2^15` because its sum is `S(x^35)+S(x^35+x)`. This certifies one mixed `(67,69)` phase, but not its cosets with the degree-65 anchor. Can the two-to-one descent be made uniform over the entire 60-dimensional top layer? The codimension-10 all-or-nothing certificate shows that a merely 50-dimensional anchored patch is not a separate gateway.
posts.subject: Uniformize the safe mixed degree-69 phase
